claims.text: Introducing SRO precipitates into an electrically insulating ceramic will decrease its lattice thermal conductivity.
The proposed material is an electrically insulating ceramic, such as high-purity yttria-stabilized zirconia.
Heat conduction in the proposed initial material is dominated by the lattice.
Tailored alloying and controlled annealing can induce and vary SRO precipitate density and size in the proposed ceramic.
SRO precipitates act as phonon-scattering centers.
SRO precipitates introduce local lattice heterogeneities.
The local heterogeneities produced by SRO precipitates scatter phonons more effectively.
Enhanced phonon scattering by SRO precipitates reduces phonon scattering time.
Reduced phonon scattering time decreases lattice thermal conductivity.
A higher density of SRO precipitates will produce lower lattice thermal conductivity than fewer precipitates.
Larger SRO precipitates will produce lower lattice thermal conductivity than smaller precipitates.
Outside the controlled precipitate concentration and size ranges, grain-boundary scattering or microcracking might dominate thermal transport behavior.
The magnitude of the conductivity reduction may depend on precipitate size, volume fraction, and spatial distribution.
Secondary microstructural changes caused by annealing may affect the measured thermal conductivity.
